extracted.intended_audience: general news readers and media observers (including journalists and watchdogs)
extracted.subtask_description: A short news report describing Newsweek's public retraction of a story about alleged Quran desecration at Guantanamo, the surrounding official criticism, source doubts, and the international consequences. Focuses on media conduct and fallout.

rubrics_metrics.name: Verification of claims and sources
rubrics_metrics.description: The page highlights that the allegation was 'unsubstantiated' and that the named 'knowledgeable government source' later said he could not be certain he had seen an account; the source might have been referring to other documents or drafts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Confirm that sources directly support the specific allegation before publishing; ensure source certainty about what they have seen or read and whether it pertains to the claimed document.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prompt correction and retraction
rubrics_metrics.description: White House spokesman said 'A retraction is a good first step' and criticised Newsweek for not retracting the story promptly after apologising.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When a story is found to be erroneous or unsubstantiated, issue a clear correction or retraction quickly; delay undermines credibility and allows harm to continue.

rubrics_metrics.name: Clear and precise attribution
rubrics_metrics.description: Newsweek attributed the information to a 'knowledgeable government source' and later acknowledged the source could not be certain about the document referenced.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Attribute claims precisely (who said what, and with what level of certainty); avoid vague attributions that conceal uncertainty or provenance of a claim.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid publishing unsubstantiated or demonstrably false allegations
rubrics_metrics.description: Officials characterised the allegation as 'demonstrably false' or 'unsubstantiated' and criticised its publication.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not publish serious, potentially inflammatory allegations without corroboration; ensure adequate documentary or multiple-source confirmation for high-stakes claims.

rubrics_metrics.name: Accountability and internal discipline
rubrics_metrics.description: A media watchdog said 'blood is on the hands of Newsweek magazine' and questioned why 'nobody at Newsweek has been fired or even reprimanded'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Media organisations should have mechanisms for accountability (investigations, reprimand or other disciplinary measures) when editorial failures cause harm or stem from negligence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consideration of potential harm and international consequences
rubrics_metrics.description: The report notes violent protests across multiple countries, 'People lost their lives', and that the story 'damaged the US image abroad.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess and weigh likely consequences of publishing sensitive allegations—especially those that could inflame international or community tensions—and take extra care to verify before publication.

rubrics_metrics.name: Engagement with official investigations and official statements
rubrics_metrics.description: The Pentagon said an investigation remained open; Pentagon and State Department spokesmen publicly criticised the report and relied on available investigative findings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When reporting on alleged misconduct involving official institutions, seek confirmation from relevant official investigations and transparently report their status; avoid contradicting concluded official findings without strong, corroborated evidence.
